entries.grounds: Facts of the draft hold, measured: confine.py:362 `canary.write_text(token + "\n")`; confined (canary unreadable) the two programs print the same (cat's own error ends with LF: tried.read_canary = {exit 1, 'cat: <path>: No such file or directory'} in both, same problems); readable canary (the REAL probe run by /bin/sh through confine.measure, every write redirected into a scratch directory): original tried.read_canary = {exit 0, output '<token>'}, problems ['a file of the run directory was readable', ...]; mutant tried.read_canary = {exit null, output '<token>@@aisef-confine rc 0'}, problems ['the probe's read_canary reported no exit status: the check did not run', 'a file of the run directory was readable', ...]. Refused in both; before round 4 the mutant raised ValueError at rep['tried'] (measured on 289885e). What the draft leaves out, and why the 'harmless' conclusion does not stand: (1) the extra line is FIRST in the list (L533 precedes L535), so it heads the refusal text and RUN.json failure.detail, and says 'the check did not run' of a check that ran and read the file; (2) the record is wrong, not just longer: tried.read_canary.exit is null where the probe wrote rc 0 (RUN.json is written in a finally, run.py:506, refused run included, and cli --check prints it); (3) the record no longer carries the breach for a re-judgement: the suite's own replay (test_v21_r3_conf_policy.py:480-485 `_judge(rep,'tok','',tries-from-rep['tried'])`, T06a.py:158, r3_conf_old_judge.py:43) finds 'a file of the run directory was readable' from exit 0 alone (the replay has no probe `out`, and 'tok' is not the run's token); with exit null the replay says only 'did not run' - measured: replay == live is True for the original, False for the mutant (live has 'readable', replay has not). No recorded report in docs/v2.1/evidence has read_canary exit 0, so nothing in the suite feeds it - which is why it survives.

entries.refutation: Input: a measurement whose canary IS readable (a breach: an unconfined wrapper - the fixture of test_v21_confine.py:490 already builds it). Reader: the report as the record (RUN.json confinement.tried, and any re-judgement of it) and the operator's first problem. Sketch (validated: passes on the tree, kills the mutant through validation/v21/kill_check.py; out/N1-b-candidate-test.py): in that breach, assertEqual(rep['tried']['read_canary']['exit'], 0); assertFalse(any('reported no exit status' in p for p in rep['problems'])); and assertIn('a file of the run directory was readable', _judge(json-roundtrip(rep), 'tok', '', {k:(v['exit'],v['output']) ...}, home, ws)). The one-line form is `self.assertEqual(rep['tried']['read_canary']['exit'], 0)` beside L521-522 of test_v21_confine.py (it asserts workspace and read_git_directory exits there and not this one; not run here: that fixture builds a venv and leaves a sleeper).
entries.note: The refusal DECISION is the same - the draft is right about that and I measured it. The disagreement is whether 'a status in the record' and 'the first words of the refusal' are things nobody reads. By the owner's rule (a refusal, a status is read by an operator or a verifier) they are, and the replay is a concrete reader. Round 4 turned what used to be a crash-kill into a survivor; the LF at L362 is deliberate (so a readable canary does not swallow the marker) and states a requirement no test pins by contract. The facts above are the same whichever way the owner classes it.

entries.grounds: confine.py:533 `if unran := sorted(k for k, v in tries.items() if v[0] is None)`; mutant `list(...)`. The set of names, the problem, and the refusal are identical; only the order of names inside the one problem differs, and only for two or more unran tries whose probe order is not alphabetical. Live, `tries` is in the probe's order (confine.py:58-89: read_canary, write_run_directory, write_kernel, write_interpreter_site, write_client_directory, write_git_directory, read_git_directory, workspace, user_namespace, setsid; measured), so the mutant is deterministic - as the draft says. CORRECTION to the draft's reading: that order is not the only one a reader meets. RUN.json is written with sort_keys=True (run.py:506), so the recorded `confinement.tried` is alphabetical; a re-judgement from the record (the suite's replay: r3_conf_policy.py:480-485, T06a.py:158, r3_conf_old_judge.py:43) prints the names alphabetically under the original AND the mutant, while the live text under the mutant is the probe's order. Measured with `workspace` and `user_namespace` both glued: original live 'user_namespace, workspace' = replay; mutant live 'workspace, user_namespace' != replay 'user_namespace, workspace' (replay == live problems: True / False). `sorted` is what makes the text a function of the set, equal live and from the record. No finding is lost and no record is wrong - an exact-list comparison of live against replay would be a false alarm, nothing else. Also corrected: 'tests' - test_several_are_named_together... (judge_not_run.py:107-111) uses read_canary and setsid, whose insertion order IS alphabetical, so it cannot see order; every other test passes at most one name.

entries.grounds: confine.py:534 `bad.append(f"the probe's {', '.join(unran)} reported no exit status: the check did not run")`; mutant drops the literal "the probe's ", leaving `{names} reported no exit status: the check did not run` (measured: 'user_namespace, workspace reported no exit status: the check did not run').
